note: The English epigraphs quote the KJV; each French epigraph is Louis Segond (1910) verbatim — the whole verse where the English quotes the whole verse, the matching Segond portion where it quotes part (Matt 10:28, Acts 5:29, Matt 7:12, Heb 13:3) — with the “(KJV)” label dropped, line-initial capitals of poetic lines lowered and a verse-final comma/semicolon closed with a full stop, as the shipped teen editions do. Psalm 51:1 (English) is Psaume 51:3 in Segond and is cited so; the rows keep English numbering.

Foxe’s archaic English quotations (Polycarp, Hus, Luther at Worms, Tyndale, Jane Grey, Latimer, Cranmer, Foxe’s 1575 plea) are rendered in a slightly classical French; Latimer’s “play the man” is « conduisez-vous en homme », Luther’s “Here I stand” is the traditional « Me voici, je ne puis faire autrement ». Wycliffe’s bedside retort is shaped to echo Psaume 118:17 (« Je ne mourrai pas, je vivrai »), which is what it alludes to (self_rendered). In ch. 7 the English phrases “Let there be light” and “the powers that be” are kept in English with their Segond wording glossed (Genesis 1:3, Romans 13:1, mined).

Names in usual French forms: Polycarpe, Smyrne, Perpétue, Félicité, Révocat, Blandine, Lyon, Jean Hus, John Wyclif (French spelling), Charles Quint, Anvers, Vilvorde, Édouard VI, Marie, Élisabeth, Cantorbéry, Rangoun, Birmanie; Ponticus, Lady Jane Grey, Ridley, Latimer, Cranmer and the Quakers’ names unchanged. The Q&A’s “The full book is also available” became « disponible (en anglais) » since no French full edition exists.

Title « Le Livre des martyrs (Pour ados) » is 32 characters — over the 28-char rail limit; the shorter « Martyrs de Foxe (Pour ados) » (27) is the fallback if the cover needs it.
